title: unknown vs any

options.t: They are identical
A value of type unknown must be narrowed (e.g. with typeof) before it can be used; any disables type checking
unknown is only for functions
any is safer

explanation: Prefer `unknown` for values from JSON, catch clauses or external input, then narrow with type guards or a schema validator (e.g. zod).

title: interface vs type alias
body: Which capability is specific to `interface` declarations?

options.t: Describing object shapes
Declaration merging: multiple declarations with the same name combine
Union types
Generics

explanation: Interfaces can be reopened (useful for augmenting library types); type aliases can express unions, intersections, mapped and conditional types. For plain object shapes either works.

title: Partial<T>

options.t: A type with all User properties required
A type with all User properties optional
A type with only the first property
A readonly copy

explanation: Related utilities: `Required<T>`, `Readonly<T>`, `Pick<T, K>`, `Omit<T, K>`, `Record<K, V>`. `Partial` is common for patch/update payloads.

title: Discriminated unions
body: Given `type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'square'; side: number }`, how does TypeScript know `shape.r` exists inside `if (shape.kind === 'circle')`?

options.t: It doesn't; you must cast
Checking the literal discriminant property narrows the union to the matching member
Because r is declared first
Runtime reflection

explanation: Add an exhaustive `switch` with a `never` check in the default branch so adding a new variant produces a compile error where it is not handled.

title: Typed property access
body: Which signature returns the correctly typed value of a property for any object?

options.t: function get(obj: any, key: string): any
function get<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]
function get<T>(obj: T, key: string): T
function get(obj: object, key: keyof object)

answer: Constrain K to keyof T and return the indexed access type T[K].
explanation: `get(user, 'age')` then has type `number`, and `get(user, 'nope')` is a compile error.
